title: Performance trace lab: find the long task
objective: Record a throttled trace, find the long task in the Main track, and show that splitting it brings INP under 200 ms.
summary: An intro video shows Live metrics and how a busy main thread delays the paint after a click. A trace simulation lets the learner switch between no throttling, 20x CPU slowdown and a split handler, and step through the tasks, the long task and the INP breakdown. A guided walkthrough pauses at the long task, the throttling comparison and the fix, and a summary video gives the routine and the good values for LCP, INP and CLS. The numbers are one example trace.

props.title: Main-thread tasks around one click (example trace)

frames.caption: Recording at 1x CPU. Each bar is one task on the main thread, in order, in milliseconds.
No task is over 50 ms, so the trace has no long task and no red triangle.
The Interactions track splits the click: 1 ms input delay, 15 ms processing, 2 ms presentation delay.
INP for this click is 1 + 15 + 2 = 18 ms, good: 200 ms or less.

inspect.label: Why only part is red
inspect.text: A task is long when it runs over 50 ms. DevTools marks it with a red triangle and shades only the part after the first 50 ms in red, so you see how far over the limit it is.

inspect.label: Three parts of INP
inspect.text: On the Interactions track, whiskers show input delay and presentation delay at both ends of the processing time. Hover the interaction to read all three numbers.

checkpoints.prompt: In one sentence: why does a long task make a click feel slow?
checkpoints.explanation: The main thread runs one task at a time, so the browser cannot paint the answer to the click until the long task ends.

checkpoints.prompt: The click handler task lasts 300 ms. Which part does the Performance panel shade red?

choices.text: The last 250 ms, the part over 50 ms

choices.misconception: Thinks the whole task is over the limit, not only the part after 50 ms
Thinks the red part is the allowed budget instead of the excess

checkpoints.explanation: A long task is any task over 50 ms. DevTools shades only the time after the first 50 ms in red, so the red length shows how much the task went over.

checkpoints.prompt: On your laptop the handler takes 15 ms. What happens to it at 20x CPU slowdown?

choices.text: It runs much longer and can become a long task
It stays at 15 ms because the code did not change
choices.misconception: Thinks task time depends only on the code, not on CPU speed
Confuses CPU throttling with network throttling

checkpoints.explanation: CPU throttling makes the CPU slower than its usual ability, so every task on the main thread takes longer. A short handler on a fast laptop can become a long task on a slow device.

checkpoints.prompt: In the simulation, keep 20x CPU and find the version of the handler whose INP is 200 ms or less. Step to its INP frame.

goal.hint: Choose the split preset, then press Forward until INP shows.

checkpoints.explanation: Splitting the work lets the handler update the page in 40 ms and yield. The browser paints before the rest runs, so processing time drops from 300 ms to 40 ms and INP from 360 ms to 100 ms.

checkpoints.prompt: The Layout shifts track shows a cluster of purple diamonds. What CLS value counts as good?

choices.misconception: Mixes up CLS with the LCP limit of 2.5 seconds
Mixes up CLS with the INP limit of 200 milliseconds

checkpoints.explanation: CLS is a score without a unit, built from the layout shifts on the Layout shifts track. A good page keeps it at 0.1 or less; 2.5 s is the LCP limit and 200 ms is the INP limit.
